title: Add a fines feature and an overdue report to a library app
prompt:
This library app has three features: catalog (books and their daily fine rate in cents), members (standard and student members) and loans (who borrowed what, due and returned dates). Add overdue fines as a new feature in src/library_app/features/fines, and an overdue report command.

The fines package (src/library_app/features/fines/__init__.py) exports fine_cents(daily_rate_cents: int, days_late: int, tier: Tier) -> int, plus whatever the composition root needs. Tier is the members feature's enum (Tier.STANDARD and Tier.STUDENT, whose values are the strings 'standard' and 'student'). The fine for one loan is days_late times the book's daily rate, capped at 20 times the daily rate (the cap applies before any discount). Students pay half of that, rounded down to a whole cent. All money is integer cents.

The overdue report covers every loan in the app's loans data as of a date given by the caller (an ISO date such as '2026-03-31'; never read the clock). A loan is late by the number of days its end date is after its due date, never negative. The end date is the return date when the loan was returned on or before the as-of date; a loan returned later than that (or not returned) is still out, so its end date is the as-of date. A loan returned late therefore keeps its final fine however far in the future the as-of date is. The fine of each loan comes from its book's daily rate (use the catalog's rate, do not copy the rate table) and its member's tier; loans whose book or member does not exist are ignored. A member's total is the sum of their loan fines.

Add overdue_report_main(as_of: str) -> None to src/library_app/composition_root.py, next to catalog_main and member_loans_main, writing to standard output, for the app's own seeded data. Each line ends with a newline. The first line is 'Overdue fines as of <as_of>'. Then one line per member whose total is more than zero, formatted '<member name>: $<dollars>.<cents>' (for example 'Ada Stone: $12.50', 'Edgar Dunn: $0.05'), ordered by total descending, then by name ascending. When no member has a fine, the second line is 'No overdue fines'. Also add the command to run(argv) in src/library_app/cli.py: run(['overdue', '<as_of>']) calls overdue_report_main, like the existing catalog, loans and member commands.

Use the catalog, members and loans features only through their package __init__.py files (from library_app.features.catalog import ...); do not change those features. The import-linter contracts in pyproject.toml check that for the existing features; leave them as they are. nitpicker flags production code that only tests call, so everything your tests import must also be used by the production code: wire fine_cents into the report, and the report into overdue_report_main and run. Add tests in tests/test_fines.py. Run nitpicker-gate until it exits 0.
